learning.title: Capture mode must match the property: a full-page shot cannot prove a viewport-relative cap
learning.body:
#479 round 4 (2026-11-17, qa-qa): the picker's 100dvh cap was "proven" by a 1440x1090 capture - but dvh is relative to the VIEWPORT, and a full-page capture makes the viewport the page, so the image cannot show the cap at all. The cap was real (qa-qa ran the app at 1440x900 and measured picker bottom=884 inside the viewport), but the PR's own evidence did not prove it: same class as the tests chased all night - evidence that reads as proof and is not.
Rule: the capture instrument must carry the property being proven, or it proves nothing: - viewport-relative properties (dvh/dvh caps, sticky headers, above-the-fold placement, fold clipping) need windowOnly: true captures, never full-page; - full-page captures answer "does anything anywhere differ" (sibling of compare-the-region-not-the-image: choose the scope that carries the property, and state which one the image is); - when an AC names a viewport property, the evidence section names the capture mode beside it, so the reviewer can see the instrument matches the claim.
Corollary: a visual AC verified by a capture whose mode cannot show it is UNPROVEN even when the underlying fix is correct - re-capture with the right mode in the same push as the fix, never "the measurement was run manually so the image is fine".
